items.question: When do you use Span versus string?
items.answer: Span is a window over existing memory — char array, stackalloc buffer, or string backing — without allocating a new string. Use Span for parsing headers, tokens, and CSV fields on hot paths. string is immutable heap object — fine for storage and API boundaries. After parsing, you may still allocate a string when you need to store the value long term.

items.sixtySeconds: Span slices without alloc. string for stored text. Memory for async fields.

items.question: When is stackalloc appropriate for CSV import?
items.answer: When you have a proven maximum line length and the scratch fits safely on the stack — typically hundreds of chars, not megabytes. Parse with span walks instead of Split. For rows or files exceeding stack limits, stream with StreamReader and use ArrayPool for large buffers to avoid Large Object Heap churn. Validate line length before stackalloc.

items.sixtySeconds: stackalloc bounded lines. Span parse. Pool or stream for huge data.

items.question: Why does SkiaSharp need using even though C# has GC?
items.answer: SkiaSharp wraps native Skia bitmaps and surfaces allocated outside the managed heap. GC only tracks the small managed wrapper. Without Dispose, native pixels stay allocated until a finalizer runs much later — looks like a memory leak under load. using releases native resources deterministically at block exit.

items.sixtySeconds: Native memory outside GC. Dispose now. Finalizer too late for bitmaps.

items.question: What is the minimum you need to know about P/Invoke?
items.answer: It is the boundary to native DLLs. Marshaling converts strings and arrays to native layout. Use official NuGet wrappers when they exist. For new declarations prefer LibraryImport source generation. Respect calling convention and charset. Pin or use Span only for the call duration. You are not writing a C++ shop — isolate interop in a small shim.
followUps: How does pinning affect GC compaction?
items.sixtySeconds: P/Invoke is native boundary. Wrappers preferred. Short pin. LibraryImport modern path.
